THE HUMAN ATLASES · DEEP DIVE

Homo neanderthalensis: Every Mapped Fossil & aDNA Locality Across Eurasia

For roughly 400,000 years, Neanderthals (Homo neanderthalensis) inhabited an immense Eurasian belt stretching nearly 7,000 km from Atlantic Portugal and Wales to Siberia's Altai Mountains, and south to Gibraltar, Sicily/Calabria, Crete-adjacent Mani, Shukbah in Palestine, and the Iranian Zagros. Here we catalogue 121 major and regional confirmed skeletal, dental, and genetic localities across 11 provinces—separating verified human remains from purely lithic Mousterian scatter sites.

All 121 mapped confirmed Neanderthal fossil and ancient-DNA localities across Western Europe, Central/Eastern Europe, Balkans, Crimea, Caucasus, Anatolia, Levant, Zagros, Central Asia, and Altai Siberia (~430–37 ka).

Eurasian fossil range from Portugal (-9.2°W) and Wales (-3.4°W) across continental Europe, Levant, and Zagros to Chagyrskaya and Okladnikov (+84.0°E) in Altai Siberia.

Emergence & Accretion: Sima de los Huesos to MIS 5e (430–120 ka)

Neanderthal nuclear DNA divergence from Denisovans dates deep into the Middle Pleistocene (>430 ka): Sima de los Huesos in northern Spain already carries early Neanderthal nuclear DNA and derived mandibles by 430 ka, accompanied by transitional European fossils at Swanscombe (~400 ka), Steinheim (~300–250 ka), Saccopastore (~250 ka MIS 7), Pontnewydd (~225 ka), Biache-Saint-Vaast and Tourville-la-Rivière (~200 ka), Ehringsdorf (~230 ka), and early Southwest Asian teeth at Qaleh Kurd (Iran) and Tabun. [122] [78] [58] [4]

By ~172–115 ka, calcified skeletons like Altamura Man (Apulia, Italy), >800 Krapina bones (Croatia, preserving white-tailed eagle talons crafted into ornaments), Scladina (Belgium, 127 ka), Hohlenstein-Stadel (Germany, 124 ka carrying an ancient ~270 ka introgressed African mtDNA lineage), Baume Moula-Guercy (~120 ka), and Stajnia (~116 ka north of the Carpathians) prove classic Neanderthals thrived across temperate interglacial Europe and simultaneously reached Denisova Cave (~120 ka Denisova 5) in Altai Siberia. [77] [123] [70] [74] [89]

Classic & Eastern Dispersals: Iberia & Doggerland to Crimea, Levant, Zagros & Altai (100–45 ka)

During MIS 5–3 glacial cycles, Neanderthals adapted across extraordinarily diverse habitats: coastal marine foraging along Portugal (Figueira Brava, Oliveira), Gibraltar, Italy (Guattari, Cavallo, Archi), and submerged Doggerland plains ('Krijn' dredged from the North Sea floor); alpine Jura caves (Cotencher); tundra hunting at 52°N Salzgitter; intentional pit burials across SW France (La Chapelle-aux-Saints, La Ferrassie, Le Moustier, Regourdou), Syria (Dederiyeh infants), Iraq (Shanidar 1–10 & Shanidar Z), Mount Carmel/Galilee (Kebara hyoid, Amud 1), open-air 'Ein Qashish, and southernmost Shukbah in Palestine. [66] [46] [107] [109] [111] [113]

Across Eastern Europe and Asia, two profound discoveries link geographically vast regions: (1) Pigott et al. (2025 PNAS) extracted an unexpected ~46 ka Neanderthal femur mitogenome from Starosele in Crimea closely matching Micoquian groups >3,000 km away at Chagyrskaya and Okladnikov in Siberia, confirming a rapid ~65–50 ka steppe migration alongside Teshik-Tash (Uzbekistan) and North Caucasus Mezmaiskaya; and (2) genetic evidence at Denisova 11 ('Denny', an F1 Neanderthal–Denisovan daughter) documents inter-lineage encounters at Eurasian crossroads. [96] [98] [118] [121]

Demographic Isolation, Overlap & Disappearance (~45–38 ka) — Scope Note on Minor Fragments

High-resolution hydroxyproline radiocarbon dating (Spy/Engis/Goyet ~44–40.6 ka, Vindija ~44–42 ka, Subalyuk ~40 ka, Sima de las Palomas ~43–40 ka, Bawa Yawan ~43–41 ka) combined with 2024 genomic sequencing of 'Thorin' from Grotte Mandrin (50,000 years isolated from contemporary late French groups!) reveals that final European Neanderthal populations splintered into tiny, genetically isolated pockets prior to ~40–39 ka, even as arriving Homo sapiens incorporated ~2% Neanderthal ancestry (captured directly in ~40 ka Peștera cu Oase 1 in Romania). [67] [59] [45] [21]

Transparency on scope: This atlas maps every major and regionally diagnostic confirmed Neanderthal skeletal, dental, and aDNA locality (121 named sites). Hundreds of additional tiny single-tooth museum fragments without firm stratigraphic dates (mostly within already mapped Dordogne/Charente/Belgian/Italian river valleys) and >1,000 purely stone-tool Mousterian sites lacking human bones are intentionally kept distinct from confirmed fossil sites. [45] [37]

(2016) single-grain OSL)Well-preserved ~2-year-old Neanderthal child skull and mandible from Layer 4 Mousterian of Acheulean Tradition (MTA Type B), directly anchored by ESR and OSL.Lacks associated postcrania; adjacent Pech IV records rich fire/manganese pigment use.[51] [37]
Okladnikov Cave (Sibiryachikha, Altai, Siberia)~50–40 thousand years ago (Krause et al. (2007 Nature) mtDNA, Kolobova (2020) & Skov/Massilani (2022–2026))Humeri, juvenile femur, and teeth associated with Sibiryachikha/Micoquian tools representing the EASTERNMOST confirmed Neanderthal skeletal fossils known on Earth (~51.7°N, 84°E)—genetically…Subadult fragmentary limbs alongside fauna; sits ~100 km northwest of Denisova Cave.[118] [98] [121]
Vindija Cave (Croatia)c. 48,000–40,000 years ago (Hydroxyproline single-amino-acid AMS redating and 30x high-coverage nuclear genome assembly of specimen Vindija 33.19.)Supplied the highest-precision genetic portrait of late European Neanderthals immediately prior to disappearance, clarifying shared ancestry (~50–45 ka) with the Neanderthals who admixed with…Cryoturbation inside karst G3/G1 boundaries mixes late Mousterian and early Upper Paleolithic split-base points unless bones are directly dated.[11] [21]
Starosele (Bakhchisarai, Crimea)~48–40 thousand years ago (Pigott et al. (2025 PNAS) ZooMS, direct 14C & mitogenome)ZooMS peptide screening of unrecognized bone splinters uncovered a new ~46–45 ka late Neanderthal femoral shaft ('Starosele 3') whose mitochondrial genome falls close to…Distinguishes authentic ~45 ka Neanderthal femur from a historically intrusive Holocene child burial at Starosele.[96]
Grotte du Renne at Arcy-sur-Cure (Yonne, France)c. 45.5–40.5 thousand years ago (High-precision collagen ultrafiltration AMS dates (Hublin 2012) paired with 2023 identification of modern-human neonate ilium.)Most celebrated European transition debate site: pierced fox-canine pendants, ring-grooved ivory pins, and bone awls in Level X, yielding both Neanderthal temporal bones/proteomes and a newly…Contested whether pendants reflect independent Neanderthal symbolism, acculturation, or fine-scale Aurignacian mixing.[22] [23] [24]
Engis Cave ('Engis 2', Awirs, Liège, Belgium)~46–40 thousand years ago (Schmerling (1833) / Devièse et al. (2021 PNAS) CSRA ~44–40.6 ka)Excavated by Philippe-Charles Schmerling in 1829—nearly 30 years BEFORE Feldhofer! Engis 2 (~4–6-year-old Neanderthal child cranium) sat unrecognized alongside Pleistocene rhino bones until…Historically commingled with Neolithic Engis 1 burial until careful fluorine/14C work separated them.[67]
Roccia San Sebastiano (Mondragone, Campania, Italy)~46–42 thousand years ago (Oxilia et al. (2022 AJPA) & ultrafiltration 14C)Direct evidence that late Neanderthal occupation and deciduous molar morphology persisted immediately prior to Campania's Upper Paleolithic technological transition.Single-cave dental assemblage.[85]
Bawa Yawan Rockshelter (Nawdarwan Valley, Kermanshah, Iran)~45–41 thousand years ago (Direct TL/OSL & Bayesian 14C (Heydari-Guran 2021 PLOS ONE; 2024))Left lower deciduous canine sealed in situ inside Zagros Mousterian levels dated ~43.6–41.5 ka cal BP just beneath early Baradostian/Upper Paleolithic layers—first stratified in situ Iranian…Single pediatric canine directly below UP transition.[117] [105]
Goyet Troisième Caverne (Gesves, Namur, Belgium)~45–40 thousand years ago (Direct collagen 14C & Rougier et al. (2016) Sci. Rep.)Largest northern European late Neanderthal fossil cluster (~99 specimens from >=5 individuals), extensively cut-marked, fractured for marrow, and fashioned into four retouchers (bone tools…Ex-situ 1868 Dupont excavation boxes reassembled via ancient DNA & direct AMS 14C.[69] [67]
Kleine Feldhofer Grotte (Neander Valley, Düsseldorf, Germany)~45–39.5 thousand years ago (AMS 14C & Schmitz et al. (2002 PNAS) 1997 cave-dump re-excavation)The August 1856 quarry discovery ('Neanderthal 1', holotype of Homo neanderthalensis, named by William King 1864). Schmitz & Thissen (1997) dramatically relocated the destroyed cave's dumped…Quarrying destroyed the original limestone cliff in 1856; all context stems from sediment screening & direct 14C/aDNA.[71] [45]
La Roche à Pierrot (Saint-Césaire, Charente-Maritime, France)~44–39 thousand years ago (TL & ultrafiltration direct collagen 14C (42–40 ka cal BP))Crushed partial adult skeleton ('Pierrette') excavated in 1979 from Châtelperronian levels, demonstrating Neanderthals persisted alongside or immediately after the arrival of Aurignacian…Minor stratigraphic mixing debate between underlying Denticulate Mousterian and Châtelperronian units.[45] [31]
Spy Cave (Betch aux Rotches, Namur, Belgium)~44–40.5 thousand years ago (Devièse et al. (2021 PNAS) hydroxyproline single-amino-acid 14C)Discovered in 1886, Spy I and Spy II proved scientifically that Neanderthals were truly fossil Pleistocene humans buried with cold-steppe fauna and Mousterian tools; 2021 compound-specific…Earlier bulk collagen 14C gave falsely young ~36 ka ages due to bovine museum glue contamination.[67] [68]
Peștera cu OaseOase 1: about 42–37 ka (Published calibrated radiocarbon range for the fossil; generations inferred independently from DNA segment lengths. Internal years use 1950 minus the quoted age in years for display; rounded geological ages are not exact calendar dates.)Long Neanderthal-derived DNA segments indicate a Neanderthal ancestor about four to six generations earlier.This individual’s approximately 6–9% estimate is not a population average; the analysis did not find substantial contribution to later sampled Europeans. Coordinates mark an approximate public locality, not a surveyed fossil position.[25]
Subalyuk Cave (Bükk Mountains, Northern Hungary)~42–38 thousand years ago (Direct ultrafiltered 14C dating (Mester et al. 2023))Adult female sacrum/teeth and ~3-year-old child cranium/mandible (Subalyuk 1 & 2); 2023 direct radiocarbon dating confirms Subalyuk among the very youngest Neanderthals in the Carpathian…Original 1932 excavation limited spatial plotting between late Mousterian sublayers.[91] [45]
